summary: Burnett County, WI DNR tower on Tower Hill (1932 per register), staffed to 2011, sold and taken down in 2020; owner planned a private rebuild at Montreal, WI. Unconfirmed since.

facts.design: 110-foot DNR fire tower with a cab on top
facts.status_note: Taken down in February 2020 and sold to a private owner, who planned to rebuild it at Montreal, WI; no source after 2020 confirms that it stands there. The original Tower Hill site is not described today.

staffing.status: staffed by Burnett County DNR until 2011

access.note: Now on private property for private use; no source describes public access. The original Tower Hill site was DNR land, and no source describes it today.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Register: built by the State of Wisconsin in 1932. Sentinel: in place since 1932 after being moved. WE ARE: constructed in 1937 on the other side of the highway, later moved. The story uses 1932 and reports the 1937 account.

Register and Sentinel: 110-foot tower. WE ARE: Dobbs put the total at about 95 feet (about 85 feet to the cab plus about 10 feet for the cab). The facts use 110 feet; the story reports the owner's figure.
Sentinel spells the buyer Jon Dobbs; WE ARE spells him John Dobbs. The story uses Jon and notes the other spelling.

notes_for_editor: The Sentinel (Feb 27, 2020) gives the 2020 sale, teardown and Montreal plan. The WE ARE article has no date in what we read, so its 1937 build date and 95-foot height are reported as that source's account. No source after 2020 confirms the tower was re-erected at Montreal, WI, and nothing describes Tower Hill today. Search turned up no later source on the rebuild; a future check of the Montreal site or a Dobbs-related report would settle it. The register's 2020 status and staffing to 2011 agree with both news reports. The Sentinel gives Dorene Snyder's time in the tower as 24 years; WE ARE dates her smoke-spotting from 1988 to 2011. The story attributes each figure to its source.
